gloss: To rise again after a setback.
teaser: Ever wondered how a mountain can symbolize a comeback?
script:
Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how a mountain can symbolize a comeback?[break 1s] The phrase is: 东山再起, dōng shān zài qǐ.[break 0.5s] 东 (dōng) means 'east'[break 0.5s] 山 (shān) means 'mountain'[break 0.5s] 再 (zài) means 'again'[break 0.5s] 起 (qǐ) means 'to rise'.[break 1s] So, the full idiom 东山再起 literally means 'to rise again from the East Mountain' and figuratively signifies a comeback after failure or setback.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] This idiom originates from the story of a famous general during the Southern Dynasties. After being defeated, he retreated to the East Mountain. Years later, he made a successful return to power, symbolizing resilience and the ability to start anew.[break 1.5s] Example 1: 他经历了很多困难，但他总是东山再起。  
He has gone through many difficulties, but he always manages to make a comeback.[break 1s] Example 2: 这位企业家在破产后东山再起，重新建立了自己的公司。  
This entrepreneur rose again after bankruptcy and rebuilt his company.[break 1s] Example 3: 她在比赛中失利，但东山再起，明年会再参加。  
She lost in the competition, but she'll rise again and participate next year.[break 1s] So, remember, 东山再起 means to rise again after a setback. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
